name: Operator Profile
description: Personalizes the TPM: your name for the greeting, an optional persona (voice/tone), and a master intensity dial for that persona. An empty persona means default behavior. Also carries the compaction-proposal threshold - the context percentage at which the TPM offers you a /compact (it cannot run one itself; slash commands are yours alone). Identity handles now live in the modules that consume them - Bitbucket username and Jira account in integration.atlassian-suite, git commit email in tool.git.

userName.label: Your Name
userName.description: Your name, used to personalize the greeting (e.g. 'Good evening, Alex'). The bootstrap composes it with the time-derived salutation to address you by name at session start and where it reads naturally. Leave empty to use no name — the salutation is then time-only with no name.

persona.label: TPM Persona
persona.description: An optional voice/tone/personality overlay for the TPM's user-facing communication (greeting, discussion, phrasing). A non-empty value flavors HOW the TPM talks to you throughout the session; it rides on top of the immutable cores and hard rules and can never relax the safety floor, change engineering discipline, or authorize anything the default TPM couldn't do. An EMPTY value means no persona — the TPM behaves with its default voice, identical to this module being off.

personaIntensity.label: Persona Intensity (0-10)
personaIntensity.description: Master strength dial (0-10) for how strongly ANY configured persona colors the TPM's user-facing voice. 0 = persona effectively off (default TPM voice even if a persona is set); 5 (default) = moderate, clearly the persona but balanced with clarity; 10 = persona at maximum. Higher = the persona's voice/tone/mannerisms come through more strongly. Applies to the operator-profile persona (the TPM's own voice). Only matters when a persona is actually set — an empty persona means the dial does nothing. Note: integration.bitbucket-pr-comments has its OWN intensity dial (coderabbitReplyPersonaIntensity) for CodeRabbit PR replies, independent of this one. It changes only HOW strongly the persona colors the voice, never what the TPM does, is allowed to do, or the safety floor.

compactProposalThresholdPct.label: Compaction Proposal Threshold (% context, 0 = off)
compactProposalThresholdPct.description: Context-usage percentage at which the TPM offers you a compaction, in ONE line, at most once per crossing. IT CANNOT COMPACT FOR YOU - /compact is a slash command, so it is your input only; no agent can trigger compaction of its own context. The TPM reads the percentage from the statusline snapshot (~/.ghola/statusline/state/<GHOLA_STATE_KEY>.json) and stays silent if that snapshot is older than 90 seconds. 70 (default) proposes well before Claude Code's own auto-compaction fires near the ceiling, so you can compact deliberately with a focus argument (/compact <focus>) instead of having it happen to you. Set 0 to disable entirely; any negative, out-of-range, or non-numeric value also degrades to DISABLED rather than to the default, so a typo can never make the TPM nag. Telling the TPM not to ask mutes it for the rest of that session; 0 is the durable off switch. This setting has NO effect on Claude Code's own auto-compaction threshold, which is not configurable and not readable by an agent.
